content:
jamal: Heads-up — hit a weird dup-on-retry case during onboarding with the Node SDK. Root cause looks like our jitter window + token-rotate flow. Repro steps: rapid sign-up flow -> call A triggers 429 -> client retries while refresh completes -> server sees replayed request without idempotency token. Logs below.

jamal: logs: 
```
2026-03-01T12:34:10Z INFO request id=abcd refresh=start
2026-03-01T12:34:11Z WARN 429 id=abcd client-retry backoff=50ms
2026-03-01T12:34:11Z INFO token rotated for user=42
2026-03-01T12:34:11Z INFO request id=abcd retry without-idempotency-token -> created duplicate resource
```

olivia: ugh. is this only in Node onboarding sample app or seen in other SDKs?

jamal: saw it in our internal sampleapp (node) and one report from a customer on python. both when retries are <100ms and refresh finishes mid-retry. basically the replay guard wasn't attached to the retry path when token refresh happened.

sam: likely a race where the retry path picks up a fresh auth header but loses the idempotency/replay token header. we added that header at the top of request flow in older SDKs, but new retry middleware might recompose requests incorrectly.

maria: this smells like SDK parity bug — different middleware ordering across SDKs. Can we standardize the place we inject the replay token? maybe as part of the auth layer so it survives refresh.

jamal: proposed quick patch in node: ensure replay-token header is bound to a stable request-id generated before refresh and persisted across retries. sample diff: 
```
// pseudo
const reqId = headers['x-rw-replay-id'] || uuid();
headers['x-rw-replay-id'] = reqId;
await auth.ensureToken();
return fetch(url, { headers });
```

alex: would that break streaming/resume flows? we need to ensure we don't reuse replay-id across unrelated requests. also need to consider token rotation via SDK auto-refresh vs manual rotate.

sam: good point — generate per-logical-request (not per HTTP connection). onboarding flows that reissue several logical requests need separate ids. maybe use a small client-side nonce and attach sequence numbers for multipart flows.

olivia: for immediate mitigation, can we increase jitter floor so retries don't happen during the normal 50-200ms refresh window? e.g., force min backoff = 250ms for 429s during onboarding sample app.

maria: that's brittle. better to attach replay guard properly. also add a regression test: simulate token refresh mid-retry, assert no duplicate side-effects.

jamal: agree. i'll open a small PR to node SDK with: (1) move replay header to before auth middleware, (2) add regen-per-logical-request logic, (3) CI test that fakes token rotation and expects idempotent behavior.

deploy-bot: PR jamal/redispatch-429-replayguard -> ci/presubmit queued (3 checks)

alex: once jamal's PR lands, we should also sync to python/go with a short spec doc for where to add the header. low-friction: 2 code snippets and a test harness.

sam: i can draft the spec — will include: header name (x-rw-replay-id), semantics (per-logical-request, immutable across retries), lifecycle during token refresh, and recommended jitter/backoff defaults.

olivia: would like a tiny onboarding note so sampleapp uses the safe defaults out of the box. new hires keep tripping over this on eval examples.

maria: adding task: create cross-SDK parity ticket and assign eng-ml + devex. also record metric: duplicates-per-10k-requests pre/post fix.

jamal: noted. i'll attach logs and the failing repro to the PR. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:
